score.note: Candidate size matches the owner boundary exactly (870/870 bytes), but the body is not byte-exact. The dominant residual is a single register/stack-allocation split: the reference keeps the 8-byte on-stack scratch buffer's address live in fp (r11) for the whole function (visible as 'mov r0,fp' / 'mov r2,fp' at every one of its ~5 call sites), while every candidate variant produced here instead spills that address to a numbered stack slot and reloads it at each use. This single difference cascades: it consumes one of the six small (sp+8..sp+28) scalar slots the reference keeps free for ownerIdPtr/roundMode/done/hasAlt/step/result, so every one of those slots lands 4 bytes higher than the reference's layout, and every load/store touching them mismatches even though the values themselves are correct. A second, independent, smaller residual is pure register-letter noise (r1 vs r2 vs r3 for the same value) scattered through the bitflag-testing chain (~lines corresponding to the L/R/U/D and shoulder-button checks) that does not look source-fixable without hand register assignment (prohibited by CONTRIBUTING.md). Two real bugs were found and fixed during this session versus the naive transplant: (1) the (sl+2)%2 toggle and the (Func_08077290(-1)!=0) boolean must be written as the literal C idiom that lets the compiler pick its own branchless neg/orr/lsr>>31 codegen, not as a plain `!= 0` comparison (which compiles to a branch on this compiler and desyncs everything downstream); (2) the L/R-shoulder page index (`*(s8*)(menu+28)`) must be read into a plain `s32` local BEFORE the +1/-1 branch, not kept as an `s8` and promoted separately in each branch -- the latter produces two redundant lsls/asrs sign-extend pairs (one per branch) where the reference does the sign-extending load once. That second fix alone took differing_halfwords from 390 to 327 and closed an 8-byte size gap (878->870).
